# laravel-action-otp

Confirm any action with a one-time code in Laravel 13. Package: jtargosz/laravel-action-otp (version 2.x). Facade: Jtargosz\ActionOtp\Facades\ActionOtp. Requires PHP 8.3+ and Laravel 13.

## When to use this package

Use it when a Laravel 13 app must verify the user with a short code sent by mail or SMS and then run a follow-up action: registration, password reset, email or phone change, login 2FA, confirming a sensitive route.

Do not use it for TOTP authenticator apps, WebAuthn passkeys, or a ready-made passwordless login screen.

## Install

composer require jtargosz/laravel-action-otp
php artisan vendor:publish --tag=action-otp-config
php artisan make:otp-action RegisterUserAction

## Concept

An OTP action is a class that implements Jtargosz\ActionOtp\Contracts\VerifiableAction with one method: handle(): mixed. send() stores the action and sends a code. verify() checks the code, deletes it and runs handle() once. The return value of handle() is the OtpResult payload.

The action waits in cache until verify(), so pass already hashed passwords (Hash::make) and never plain secrets.

class RegisterUserAction implements VerifiableAction
{
    public function __construct(public string $name, public string $email, public string $passwordHash) {}
    public function handle(): mixed { return User::create([...]); }
}

## Binding (important)

Each send() creates a challenge. Lookup order on verify/peek/resend/clear: withChallenge($token), then the browser session, then (only for actions with #[AnyDevice]) the last pending action of that identifier and purpose. Without a challenge the result is empty and no attempt is counted.

Browser apps: call send() and verify() from routes with the web middleware. Nothing else needed.
API clients: return $result->challenge from send() and call ->withChallenge($challenge)->verify($code).

## API

ActionOtp::to(string|int $identifier) scopes to an identifier. Normalize it first (strtolower emails).
->for(string $purpose) scopes to a purpose, default "default". Several purposes can be pending at once. A challenge from one purpose never works for another.
->withChallenge(?string $token) uses the token from send() instead of the session.
->send(VerifiableAction $action, object $notifiable): OtpResult with status sent and challenge, or throttled during send cooldown or lockout.
->verify(string $code): OtpResult; verified with payload, or empty, mismatch, expired, throttled.
->peek(string $code): OtpResult; matched without running handle() and without deleting the code.
->resend(): OtpResult; sent with a new code and the same challenge, or empty, or throttled.
->clear(): void; deletes the pending code only. Counters, lockout and cooldown stay.

Codes are strings: leading zeros are kept, whitespace is trimmed, letter codes are case-insensitive.

OtpResult: status (Jtargosz\ActionOtp\Support\OtpStatus), message (translated string), payload (mixed), challenge (string|null, set by send()). Methods: ok() true when verified, found() true when matched or verified, toArray().

OtpStatus values: sent, matched, verified, empty, mismatch, throttled, expired, device_mismatch.

Throttling is per identifier across all purposes and codes: max_attempts wrong tries in one hour lock for throttle_seconds; send_cooldown between sends. Only a successful verify resets counters, lockout and cooldown.

Standard pattern:

$result = ActionOtp::to($email)->for('register')->verify($code);
if (! $result->ok()) { return response()->json(['message' => $result->message], 422); }
$user = $result->payload;

## Per action attributes

Namespace Jtargosz\ActionOtp\Attributes, on the action class, inherited by subclasses:
#[Ttl(10)] minutes, #[CodeFormat('alphanumeric')], #[CodeLength(8)], #[SendWith(CodeSms::class)], #[AnyDevice].
#[AnyDevice] drops the session binding: the code and link work from any device. Only for low risk actions, never for password reset, email change or login.

## Examples

Register:
ActionOtp::to($email)->for('register')->send(new RegisterUserAction($name, $email, Hash::make($password)), Notification::route('mail', $email));
$result = ActionOtp::to($email)->for('register')->verify($code);

Login 2FA:
ActionOtp::to($user->email)->for('login')->send(new ConfirmLoginAction($user->id), $user);
$result = ActionOtp::to($user->email)->for('login')->verify($code);

Password reset:
ActionOtp::to($email)->for('password-reset')->send(new ResetPasswordAction($email, Hash::make($password)), Notification::route('mail', $email));

API client:
$token = ActionOtp::to($email)->for('login')->send($action, $user)->challenge;
ActionOtp::to($email)->for('login')->withChallenge($token)->verify($code);

Validation rule (uses peek, does not consume the code, a wrong code counts as an attempt):
new Jtargosz\ActionOtp\Validation\ValidOtpCode($email, 'register', $challengeOrNull)

## Routes (optional)

ActionOtp::routes($prefix = 'otp', $middleware = ['web']) registers:
POST otp/verify (action-otp.verify; identifier, code, purpose, challenge), POST otp/resend (action-otp.resend), GET and POST otp/link (signed magic link), GET otp/confirm, POST otp/confirm, POST otp/confirm/resend (auth, for otp.confirm).
JSON responses: {status, message} with 200, 409 device_mismatch, 422, 429. Payload is never serialized unless handle() returns a Responsable or Response. Web: redirect to intended URL or back with a code error. Replace by binding Jtargosz\ActionOtp\Contracts\VerifyResponse.
Rate limit: rate_limit requests per minute per IP.

Magic link: set link.enabled (ACTION_OTP_LINK=true), call ActionOtp::routes() and ActionOtp::linkView('view.name') (data: url, purpose). GET only shows the page, the form POST to $url verifies. Works in the starting browser, elsewhere status device_mismatch unless #[AnyDevice].

otp.confirm middleware: like password.confirm with a code. ActionOtp::confirmView('view.name') (data: submitUrl, resendUrl). ActionOtp::confirmUsing(fn ($user) => $user->phone) optional. JSON 423 when unconfirmed. Lasts confirm_timeout seconds. Jtargosz\ActionOtp\Http\Middleware\RequireOtpConfirmation::using($route, $seconds).

## Notifications

Default Jtargosz\ActionOtp\Mail\CodeMail: translated markdown mail, queued, encrypted, view publish tag action-otp-views.
Custom notification: extends Illuminate\Notifications\Notification with __construct(public Jtargosz\ActionOtp\Support\OtpMessage $otp). OtpMessage: code, expiresAt, purpose, link, smsText(?string $host). Set globally in config notification or per action with #[SendWith].
smsText() ends with the line "@host #code" for iOS and Android autofill. Host from sms_host, then app.url.

## Config

config/action-otp.php keys with defaults: code_format numeric (numeric, alpha, alphanumeric), code_length 6 (1-64), ttl_minutes 15, expired_grace_minutes 5, max_attempts 5, throttle_seconds 60, send_cooldown 30, store_prefix action-otp:, notification CodeMail, channels ['mail'], sms_host null, link.enabled false, rate_limit 10, confirm_timeout 900, redirects.verified /.

Env: ACTION_OTP_FORMAT, ACTION_OTP_LENGTH, ACTION_OTP_TTL, ACTION_OTP_GRACE, ACTION_OTP_ATTEMPTS, ACTION_OTP_THROTTLE, ACTION_OTP_COOLDOWN, ACTION_OTP_PREFIX, ACTION_OTP_SMS_HOST, ACTION_OTP_LINK, ACTION_OTP_RATE_LIMIT, ACTION_OTP_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT.

## Testing

ActionOtp::fake('123456') (or fake() for random codes) records sends instead of delivering notifications; storage, sessions and throttling stay real.
ActionOtp::assertSent(Action::class, fn ($action, $message, $identifier, $purpose) => ...), assertSentTimes, assertNotSent, assertNothingSent, assertVerified(Action::class, fn ($action, $payload) => ...), assertNotVerified.
ActionOtp::codeFor($identifier, $purpose = 'default'), challengeFor(...), messageFor(...).

## Artisan, events, translations

Command: php artisan make:otp-action {Name} generates App\OtpActions\{Name}. Option --force overwrites.

Events (no code, no action): Jtargosz\ActionOtp\Events\CodeSent(identifier, purpose, expiresAt), CodeVerified(identifier, purpose, payload), CodeFailed(identifier, purpose).

Translations: en, pl, it, es, de, fr, pt, nl for statuses, mail and SMS, following the app locale. Publish tag action-otp-lang, overrides in lang/vendor/action-otp/{locale}/action-otp.php.

## AI tools

Optional, needs laravel/ai. Jtargosz\ActionOtp\Ai\ResendOtpTool($identifier, $purpose = 'default', $challenge = null) and Jtargosz\ActionOtp\Ai\CheckOtpTool($identifier, $purpose, $challenge). The identifier comes from your code, the model supplies only the code. CheckOtpTool uses peek and never runs the action.

## Upgrading from 1.x

See UPGRADE.md: session or challenge binding, string codes, OtpMessage for notifications, events without code, new StoresCodes contract, renamed AI tools.
